info.title: Big Ball Sports API
info.description:
Unified sports data API (REST + GraphQL + WebSocket) aggregating 19+
free-tier upstream sources and 10 MCP scrapers behind a Stripe-style
gateway. Every response carries a confidence score and source attribution
so callers can render appropriate caveats.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Big Ball Sports API key. Or pass via `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Stripe-style idempotency token. Retries with the same key within
24h replay the original response without re-running the handler.

RateLimited.description:
Rate limited (`429`). Two causes share `error.code: rate_limited` and are
told apart by `error.message` and headers:
  - **Quota exhaustion** (per-minute or per-day cap). The envelope is
    enriched: `suggested_fix` names the next tier and its cap, and
    `meta.current_usage` + `meta.upgrade_path` carry live usage and the
    upgrade target. `X-RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Reset` are present.
  - **4xx circuit breaker** (sustained high 4xx rate — malformed
    requests, or ignoring Retry-After and hammering past quota — key in
    cooldown). Carries `X-RateLimit-4xx-Cooldown`; no `upgrade_path`.
Additive: existing parsers keying on `error.code`, `error.message`,
`docs_url`, `support`, `meta.request_id` are unaffected.
`X-RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Reset` are returned on every authenticated
response (2xx/4xx/5xx), not only on 429s, so clients can self-throttle.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the limit (or 4xx cooldown) resets.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the tighter bucket.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix seconds at which the tighter bucket resets.

X-RateLimit-4xx-Cooldown.description: Seconds remaining on the 4xx breaker cooldown (only on breaker 429s).

message.example: Daily quota exhausted (1000 of 1000 requests used)

suggested_fix.example: Pace requests using the Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* response headers — handling guide: https://bigballsdata.com/docs/rate-limits. If you're regularly at this ceiling, the solo plan is $19/month and raises your daily limit to 10,000/day: https://bigballsdata.com/dashboard/billing?plan=solo.

upgrade_path.description:
The upgrade target for THIS 429 — the next tier up the
ladder, because the caller's problem is volume.
`recommended_tier` is null at the top self-serve tier.

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Service temporarily unavailable (`503`). Returned when a backing query
exceeds the endpoint's `statement_timeout` (Postgres cancels it) instead
of holding the connection for seconds. Transient under heavy load —
retry after a short delay. Standard error envelope with
`error.code = upstream_unavailable`.

NflPlayerWeekStat.description:
One player's stat line for one game-week. All stat fields are returned
for every row regardless of position: a quarterback row carries 0 or
null in the defensive columns, a linebacker row carries 0 or null in
the passing columns.

Defensive columns are sourced from the nflverse weekly player file
(CC BY 4.0) and cover 2020 onward at the same grain as the offensive
ones.

**TACKLE TOTALS WILL NOT MATCH `/v1/stored/matches/{id}/stats`, and that
is expected.** nflverse publishes three tackle counts and no combined
total: `tackles_solo`, `tackle_assists` (assisted tackles the player
took part in) and `tackles_with_assist` (a much smaller, separate
count). The other endpoint serves a single `totalTackles` from a
different provider, at per-match rather than per-game-week grain, over
a different set of seasons.

We do NOT derive a combined total here. The usual definition is solo +
assisted, but the exact relationship between nflverse's three counts
was not verified against a reference box score, and a plausible number
computed from an unverified relationship is worse than no number — it
is indistinguishable from a correct one. Add `tackles_solo` and
`tackle_assists` yourself if you need a total, knowing that is your
definition rather than ours.

team.description: Team abbreviation the player suited up for that week.

season.description: Season LABEL — the year the season starts in.

fantasy_points_ppr.description: Standard PPR: 1/reception, 0.1/rush-rec yard, 0.04/pass yard, 6/TD, -2/int or fumble lost.

interceptions.description:
DEPRECATED and ALWAYS NULL. The loader read a column nflverse does
not publish, so this was never written in any of 112,333 rows. The
key is retained only so existing clients do not break. Read
`interceptions_thrown` or `interceptions_caught`, which say which
one they mean.

interceptions_thrown.description: Interceptions thrown by this player — the quarterback turnover stat.

interceptions_caught.description: Interceptions caught by this player — the defensive takeaway stat.

tackles_solo.description: Unassisted tackles. Not a combined total — see the schema description before comparing against totalTackles elsewhere.

tackle_assists.description: Assisted tackles this player participated in. Not interchangeable with tackles_with_assist.

tackles_with_assist.description: Tackles made WITH an assist from a team-mate. A much smaller count than tackle_assists.

tackles_for_loss.description: Tackles made behind the line of scrimmage.

tackles_for_loss_yards.description: Yards lost by the offence on those tackles.

sacks.description: Sacks credited. FRACTIONAL — a shared sack is credited as 0.5 to each defender.

sack_yards.description: Yards lost on this player's sacks. Fractional for the same half-credit reason as sacks.

fumbles_forced.description: Fumbles forced. Forcing is not recovering; recoveries are not currently served.

interception_yards.description: Return yards on this player's interceptions. MAY BE NEGATIVE — a return can be tackled behind the catch point.

defensive_tds.description: Touchdowns scored on defence. Distinct from passing_tds / rushing_tds / receiving_tds on the same row.

defensive_two_point_attempts.description: Two-point conversion returns attempted by the defence.

defensive_two_point_conversions.description: Two-point conversion returns scored by the defence.

source.description: Opaque source-tier label. Customers never see the vendor identity.

value.description: The canonical value for this field. Shape varies by FieldKey.

not_outs.description: Innings ended undismissed (includes retired hurt / retired not out).

average.description: runs / dismissals. null when never dismissed.

strike_rate.description: Runs per 100 balls. null when no balls faced are recorded.

fifties.description: Scores of 50–99. A hundred counts only in `hundreds`.

overs.description: Cricket notation, e.g. "206.4" — 206 overs and 4 balls. Derived from balls_bowled.

average.description: runs conceded / wickets. null when wicketless.

economy.description: Runs conceded per over. null when no balls bowled.

strike_rate.description: Balls per wicket. null when wicketless.

best_bowling.description: Best innings figures as wickets/runs, e.g. "5/23". null when wicketless.

message.example: One or more query parameters are invalid.

validation_errors.description: Structured field errors (e.g. a zod flatten) when applicable.

suggested_fix.description: A concrete corrected request, present only when unambiguously inferable.
suggested_fix.example: Lower limit to 200 or less, optionally add ?page=2 to page through results.

upgrade_path.description:
Present ONLY on the two errors where upgrading is the literal
fix: the quota `429` and a plan-gate `403 forbidden`. Absent on
every other error, including the `403 key_paused` reactivation
error — a paused key is reactivated, not bought.

UpgradePath.description:
The machine-readable half of an upgrade prompt: what to buy, what it
costs, and where to buy it. Identical in shape on the quota `429` and
the plan-gate `403`, so one parser handles both — but note the two
recommend DIFFERENT things, correctly. The 429 recommends the next tier
UP (the problem is volume); the 403 recommends the LOWEST tier that
unlocks the endpoint (the problem is access), so a free key blocked on
an Edge route is pointed at Edge, never at Solo.

Every figure is real: `price` is the published list price and
`daily_limit` is the cap the gateway actually enforces. Nothing here is
computed from a per-request rate, and there is no urgency or scarcity
framing anywhere in these bodies.

current_tier.description: The caller's tier at the time of the error.

recommended_tier.description:
Null only where there is nothing to recommend — the top of the
self-serve ladder on a 429.

price.description:
Monthly list price. Null for a tier that is quoted rather than
listed (Enterprise), in which case `url` is the pricing page rather
than a checkout link.

daily_limit.description: Requests/day granted by `recommended_tier`; null if unmetered.

url.description:
Checkout, deep-linked to `recommended_tier`, whenever there is a
listed price to buy. Falls back to the pricing page when there is
not — we never deep-link a purchase that cannot complete.

CanonicalId.description: BigBalls canonical id. Format `bb_<entity>_<10-32 lowercase base32 chars>`.

metric.description: Canonical metric name from a closed set.

FixtureTeamStatistics.description:
Post-match team stat line for one team. All stat fields are
nullable — a metric a league doesn't track is null, and `expected_goals`
(xG) is present only on covered leagues. Counts are integers; percentages
and xG are numbers.

round.description: Competition segment as the source names it, e.g. "Regular Season - 2" or "Group Stage". This is the axis to group gameweek analytics by: a postponed fixture keeps its round while its start_time moves by weeks, so bucketing by date splits one gameweek and merges another. Free text rather than an integer, because the phase carries meaning an integer would discard. Null where the source supplies none — currently populated for soccer only.

results.description: Position ranking. Empty until the results worker has processed the session.

secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 secret. Shown once at creation.

Per-league leaderboard sourced from our soccer_player_season_stats
(season aggregates), summing a player across their team
rows in the season. Flat data[] shape: rank, player_name, team, goals,
assists, minutes, matches (matches = season appearances). Supports a

get.description:
Per-league season xG leaderboard for the big-five European leagues,
2014 through the current season. Ranks players by expected goals and
exposes the surrounding shot-quality picture: xG, xA, npxG, xGChain,
xGBuildup, plus goals, assists, shots, key passes, matches and minutes.
`goals_above_xg` (goals minus xG) is derived for finishing over- and
under-performance.

LEAGUE-LEVEL ONLY. Rows are keyed by player NAME, not by a BigBalls
`player_id` — the xG-to-players entity bridge is not built yet,
so a per-player or per-match xG surface would serve a mostly-empty
join. Those endpoints are not offered until that bridge lands; see
docs/scoping/soccer-xg-bridge.md. Season rows we cannot attribute to a
league are excluded, so this leaderboard only ever reflects players in
the league you asked for.

`team` is the source team title verbatim and may be a comma-separated
list for a player who transferred mid-season. Refreshed daily;
5-minute Redis cache keyed by league+season+stat+min_minutes+limit.

get.summary: Player stats for a season + league
get.description:
**Baseball responses carry a `level` field. Read it before summing anything.**

- `level: "match"` — `batting`/`pitching` are totals folded from real
  per-game box scores. 2026 onward.
- `level: "season"` — no per-game box scores exist for the seasons
  asked for. The numbers are full-season aggregates and are returned in
  `seasons[]`, each entry additionally marked `level: "season"`.
  `batting`/`pitching` are `null`.
- `level: "mixed"` — both are present. `batting`/`pitching` (per-game
  derived) and `seasons[]` (season aggregates) cover **disjoint**
  periods; adding them together double-counts nothing but conflates two
  different grains. Treat them separately.

A season aggregate has no home/away dimension, so `?split=home|away`
returns no `seasons[]` entries rather than full-season totals that
ignore the filter. Fields a source cannot supply (e.g. pitch counts,
which season-level history does not carry) are **omitted**, never
returned as `0`.

get.summary: What we hold, per sport and league — the discovery catalogue
get.description:
The catalogue an agent reads to decide whether a dataset exists here, precomputed on a schedule and served from a snapshot. Every league we hold appears with its match counts, seasons, freshness and per-datatype coverage.

VOCABULARY. `data_types` is the stable default and does not change. `?v=2` adds `data_types_v2` beside it, which answers questions about a GRAIN rather than a datatype: "do you have xG" is a v1 question, "do you have PER-PLAYER xG" is a v2 one. In v2 each measure carries its grains (subject x period, e.g. `team.match` or `player.season`), every grain declares the denominator its figures count, and `not_applicable` names measures that CANNOT apply to a league as distinct from ones we simply lack. `data.vocabulary` echoes which shape was served.

v2 is opt-in because the summary answers most questions and the nested shape is only needed for grain questions. An unrecognised `?v=` serves v1 rather than failing: a catalogue call is discovery, and a query-string typo should not 400.

parameters.name: sport
parameters.description: Narrow to one sport or league; accepts any registry alias. Unknown values are a 400, never a silent empty.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Set to `2` to include `data_types_v2` (grains, denominators, not_applicable) alongside the unchanged `data_types`. Omit for the stable v1 shape.

get.description:
Injury reports by sport. What a row MEANS differs by league, because
injury data is a reporting artifact and leagues differ in what they
compel teams to disclose:

- `american_football` — the NFL's **mandated** weekly injury report
  (nflverse, CC BY 4.0). `status` is a league-defined game designation:
  Out / Doubtful / Questionable. `comment` carries practice
  participation. `player.position` is always present. Published per
  week; `meta.as_of` is the date of the games that week's report covers.
  **No `return_date`**: the NFL report is designation-based and states
  no expected return, so the field is omitted rather than sent as a
  permanent null. Only rows carrying a game designation are returned —
  a player logging a full practice with no designation is not injured,
  and is not listed.
- `basketball`, `ice_hockey` — NBA / NHL reports from a paid aggregator
  (`aggregator-paid`). Note the NHL requires no disclosure at all, so
  NHL detail is vague at the league ("upper-body"), not at this API.
- `football` — soccer absences from a paid aggregator
  (`aggregator-paid`). Mostly
  **retrospective**: a record that a player missed a fixture that has
  been played, which includes non-injury absences such as suspension.
  `meta.as_of` is the newest matchday held.
- `baseball`, and everything else — not served; returns 400 naming the
  sports that are.

Endpoints that serve a stored snapshot always carry `meta.as_of` (the
currency of the DATA, never the time we last ingested it) and set
`meta.stale: true` with a plain-language `meta.message` when no fresher
data exists yet — e.g. between seasons.

post.summary: Register a webhook subscription — NOT AVAILABLE, returns 501
post.description:
Registration is closed. Webhook DELIVERY was never wired to anything, so no webhook has ever been sent and none would be sent to an endpoint registered today. Accepting a registration would promise traffic that never arrives, which is worse than not offering the feature, so this returns 501 rather than 201. Decision recorded 2026-09-01.

For live updates today use the WebSocket feed at wss://api.bigballsdata.com/live (Pro plan and above), or poll the REST API. GET /v1/webhooks and DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id} remain available so any existing registration can still be listed and removed.

get.summary: Who played in an NBA game (box-score derived availability)
get.description:
Home/away player arrays with `min_played` and a derived `played`
boolean, from post-game box scores. Self-teaching: every response's
`meta` block carries these same semantics so the payload explains
itself.

- `data_type: post_game_participation` — this is "who played", a
  strong historical availability signal for modeling. It is NOT a
  pre-tip lineup (for true pre-tip lineups, 2025-26 onward, use
  /v1/nba/games/{id}/lineups).
- Semantics: arrays contain ONLY players who logged minutes. A
  player who is absent did not play — DNP (coach decision),
  inactive, or injured — and this endpoint cannot distinguish those
  reasons. Absence never appears as `played: false`.
- Coverage: seasons 2019-20 through 2025-26 (box-score era). Games
  before 2019-10-22, preseason and All-Star games are not covered.
- For true pre-tip availability on current and upcoming games,
  cross-reference GET /v1/injuries?sport=nba (league-wide active
  injury reports) or GET /v1/players/{id}/injury. Historical
  pre-tip injury reports do not exist at our source.
- `starter` is true/false only for games with lineup coverage
  (2025-26 onward), null for earlier games; historical starter data
  does not exist at our source and we will not fabricate it.

`id` accepts a canonical match UUID or a 10-digit NBA-stats game id
(bridged via the games list's `match_id`). A real game outside
coverage returns 200 with empty arrays and
`meta.availability_available: false`; 404 only when the id resolves
to nothing.

get.summary: Historical odds snapshots for a match (CLV)
get.description:
Every historical odds snapshot (opening / t24h / closing — never the live
`current` series) for one match, newest snapshot first, with sportsbook
names resolved. Powers closing-line value (CLV) and line-movement analysis.
Requires an Edge plan or higher (Free / Solo / Trio receive 403).
Each row carries an EVIDENCE-BASED `verification` field from two-source
cross-checking — a "verified" status is only ever returned when we
actually compared two providers, never inferred from the absence of a
check: `two_source_agreed` (both providers priced this book/market/side
and agreed — a positive comparison is on record), `two_source_diverged`
(both priced it and disagreed — `divergence_categories` then lists the
categories, e.g. `["PRICE_DIFF","STALE"]`), `single_source` (only one
provider carries this book/side, or the book has no cross-provider match
— NOT verified), or `unverified` (we have not compared this line — NOT
verified). The default when we lack evidence is `single_source` or
`unverified`, never a badge. `verified_at` dates the comparison the status
came from (null when nothing was compared) — a verification you cannot
date is a claim you cannot check. A comparison only describes the snapshot
whose line it actually compared and only within 48h of it, so a snapshot
whose price has since moved reads `unverified` rather than inheriting an
older badge. Response: `{ data: [{ match_id, snapshot_type,
snapshot_at, market, book: { id, name, logo_url }, line, source,
fetched_at, verification, verified_at, divergence_categories? }], meta: {
total, limit, offset, snapshot_types_present, generated_at } }`.

get.description:
Per (match, market, canonical book) disagreements between our two odds
providers, as detected by the divergence
worker. Categories: `PRICE_DIFF` (same line, juice differs > threshold),
`LINE_DIFF` (different line value), `MISSING_FROM_ONE` (a book one
provider doesn't carry), `STALE` (one feed lagging). Requires an Edge
plan or higher (Free / Solo / Trio receive 403). Provide `match_id`, or
else `date_from` + `date_to` to bound the kickoff window. Response: `{
data: [{ match_id, sport_type, league, kickoff_utc, market, canonical_id,
book_display_name, category, secondary_categories, magnitude, detected_at
}], meta: { total, limit, offset, categories_present, generated_at } }`.
`magnitude` is category-specific (price_diff_pct for PRICE_DIFF, line_diff
for LINE_DIFF, else null) and is an ABSOLUTE difference — it carries no
direction and cannot be used to reconstruct either provider's line. The
per-provider line and price values are deliberately not returned: the
product here is the computed disagreement, not the upstream feeds.
Returns 503 while the divergence worker is still provisioning (its table
not yet created).

Outdoor weather at an enclosed stadium describes the car park, not the game, so it is withheld rather than served. `venue.roof` is returned so a consumer can render "Indoor" instead of a blank.

A `retractable` roof is withheld on the same grounds: the roof's STATE at a given kickoff is a property of the match, we have no source for it, and a guess is indistinguishable from a fact in the response.

get.description: Who am I — the account behind the calling API key: plan, effective rate limits, a masked key id, and the GitHub-linked / paused flags. Authed by your own key (not a dashboard session), so the answer is always scoped to the key that asked. No parameters.

key_id.description: Masked: an ellipsis + the last 4 chars of the key id.

email.description: Owner email, omitted when the key has none on file.

plan.description:
The EFFECTIVE plan — what this key can actually reach, and what
`limits` below describes. Equal to the billed plan except while a
referral grant is active, in which case `billed_plan` and
`referral_grant` are also present.

The ladder actually sold is `free` → `solo` → `multi` →
`edge` → `pro` → `enterprise`. Note `multi` is the stored slug
for the tier sold as **Trio** — the display name changed, the
slug deliberately did not, so no stored row had to move. `max`
is an internal comped tier, never self-serve.

`starter`, `growth` and `business` are **deprecated**: retired
from sale, never returned for a key created today, and excluded
from every upgrade path the gateway builds. They stay enumerated
because nothing in the schema prevents a legacy row from still
holding one, and an enum that rejects a value the API can really
emit fails closed on a live customer — a worse outcome than a
wide enum. Treat them as read-only history; do not send a user
to one.

billed_plan.description:
What the account is BILLED for. Present only while a referral
grant is raising `plan` above it; absent otherwise, when `plan` is
already the billed plan. `plan` stays the effective value because
it is what the caller can actually use and what the `limits`
beside it describe.

Same value set as `plan` above, deprecated tiers included — a
legacy row is precisely the kind of account that can still be
billed for a tier we no longer sell.

referral_grant.description: A time-boxed plan grant earned through the referral program. Present only while one is active. Not a subscription — it has no price and no invoice, and when it ends the account returns to `billed_plan` with nothing removed from that plan.

plan.description: The granted plan — the same value `plan` reports while it is active.

get.description: Your key's own quota and usage: live remaining quota for today and this minute (from the rate-limit counters) plus a 7-day per-day request + 4xx-error history (from usage_events). Authed by your own key. The recent[] history is empty when the gateway is running without its Postgres pool. Answers "am I rate-limited / how much have I used" without a support round-trip.
